messages.author: 495d67130a446b65
messages.subject: Warning related with psi matrix
parts:
Hello.

I am trying to fit a sem model with blavaan. Everything appears to work, but the following warning appears:

Warning: blavaan WARNING: As specified, the psi covariance matrix is neither diagonal nor unrestricted, so the actual prior might differ from the stated prior. See https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.08667

I read the referenced paper and I would like to test the third solution suggested (Combining LKJ with Informative Priors), the one explained here: http://srmart.in/informative-priors-for-correlation-matrices-an-easy-approach/

Is it possible to implement this solution in blavaan or it is necessary to implement it directly in Stan?

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Warning related with psi matrix
parts:
Armel,

I hope to make future progress in blavaan here, but it is not automatically available at the moment.

To implement that solution, one possibility is to export blavaan's Stan file using mcmcfile = TRUE, then edit the priors (around line 925). I could provide more input if needed, but many people shy away from that Stan file because it is written for general SEM, so takes some time to get oriented.

On the other hand, unless you are doing something with Bayes factors or with prior predictive distributions, you might be able to safely ignore the warning.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Warning related with psi matrix
parts:
Hello, 

Likewise, I am obtaining this same warning message in some univariate latent change score models (LCSM). I read the paper recommended in the warning message, but I am still not clear on what blavaan is doing when this issue occurs. Is it automatically selecting a different prior, and if so, is there a way to access the prior it chooses? The models show no other signs of convergence issues. I'm assuming the warning pertains to the covariance of the intercept and slope in the LCSMs since that's the only covariance being estimated (those are the only elements listed as estimated in the psi matrix)? I'm not using Bayes factors, but I am using informative priors in most parts of the models, so I do care about the specific values of the priors.

Thanks!
Garret

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Warning related with psi matrix
parts:
Garret,

You might run the model with prisamp = TRUE, which draws samples from the priors. This could show you what the priors look like after taking into account positive definite constraints. The only affected priors would be the ones on the correlations within the psi matrix (which lead to covariances); instead of uniform from -1 to 1, they sometimes have more density around 0 to respect positive definite.

There is a recent bug that I fixed here; if it crashes for prisamp = TRUE, then also add meanstructure = TRUE to get it to run.

For the LCSM, there is a decent chance that this is a false alarm. I could say more if you send the output of

lavInspect(fit, 'est')$psi

where fit is your fitted model.

Ed
